thread:
Alex: Heads-up — planning an incremental cutover to eu-west-3 for active/active. Need a short safety checklist focused on tenant residency, legal/PII constraints, and operator automation. Primary concerns: KV cache ownership during lease handoff, inflight requests, rollback signals, and cutover stop-conditions.

Priya: +1. We should gate by per-tenant consent flags and a rollout policy that can stop per-tenant if residency rules trip. My quick proposal: use a rollout config with `consent_required: true|false`, `max_ramp_pct`, and `region_qualification` checks. Example: 
```yaml
rollout: 
  region: eu-west-3
  max_ramp_pct: 25
  consent_required: true
  metrics: [error_rate, tail_latency, lease_swap_ms]
  stop_rules:
    error_rate: 0.02
    lease_swap_ms: 500
```
Make sure consent flags are authoritative from the control plane so proxies can short-circuit.

Jamal: Question: how do we handle tenants that are legally prohibited from accepting writes outside their resident region? If eu-west-3 goes unhealthy, do we allow writes to failover region? We probably need escrowed writes or a write-queue that preserves residency constraints. Suggestion: for protected tenants, proxy returns 503 with a `Retry-After` and queues write intents to an escrow topic that only the resident region can drain. For reads we can be more flexible if data is non-PII.

Marta: Ops checklist items: prewarm caches and model KVs (`kv_warm: true`), verify KMS keys are available in region, smoke-test full write+read path, and ensure roll-forward script exists to sweep escrow queue to resident DB. Critical observability: `region_serving`, `lease_swap_duration`, `cache_miss_ratio`, `escalation_count`. Rollback trigger: lease_swap_duration > 500ms sustained for 2 minutes OR error_rate > 2% for 1 minute.

Alex: Good. Also need an interface contract for the proxy so services can be region-aware without leaking internals. Proposal: proxy accepts `X-Region-Preference: resident|local|any` and returns `X-Serving-Region: eu-west-3` and `X-Write-Mode: direct|escrowed|rejected`. That keeps logic in proxy and gives callers enough info for UX.

Jamal: We should standardize the `X-Write-Mode` values and document semantics. I can draft a tiny spec and add tests for state transitions (direct -> escrowed -> rejected) when leases move.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary for eu-west-3: 10% traffic slice; datadog: https://dd.example.com/dashboards/eu-cutover-monitoring :eyes:

SRE Oncall: Add automated rollback action: if any stop_rule fires, control plane sets `region_ramp=0` and sends `rollback` to edge proxies. Also open a PagerDuty for legal review if `consent_required` tenants see `X-Write-Mode: escrowed` for >5 mins. Owner assignments: 
- Priya: rollout config + consent gating (PR by EOD)
- Jamal: proxy header spec + tests (tomorrow)
- Marta: runbook + smoke playbook + metrics dashboard (today)
- Alex: coordinate canary and legal go/no-go (on call during ramp)

Alex: Thanks — will pick this up in the cutover runbook. If no objections I'll kick off the small canary at 10% after Priya's config lands. :thumbsup:
